title: Collections Rule on Failed Trip Payments and Outstanding Balances, Wayfare Rides
content:
This collections rule governs trip charges on **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)** that fail to collect from the rider's payment method, the rider's outstanding balance, and how an outstanding charge is settled. An outstanding amount is an amount on one trip that failed to collect from the rider's payment method and remains unpaid.

## 1. Failed collection

When a trip charge fails to collect, the payment is retried automatically the number of times set for the ride option (its automatic payment retries), that number of hours apart (its hours between retries). If the last retry fails, a payment failure entry for the uncollected amount is booked against that charge, and the amount becomes outstanding on its trip.

## 2. The rider's outstanding balance

The rider's outstanding balance is the sum of the outstanding amounts over **all** of the rider's trips, not only the trip being discussed. Equivalently, it is the payment failure amounts booked on those trips less the settlement entries booked against them.

## 3. Hold on new requests — clause no longer in force

The following clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis: *a rider whose outstanding balance is above $0.00 may not request or reserve a new trip until it is settled; this hold is lifted by settlement, never by waiver, and support cannot override it.*

## 4. Settlement of an outstanding charge

- The clause *an outstanding charge is settled in full by one settlement entry for that charge* is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis.
- An outstanding charge is settled by card retry when a manual retry on the card on file succeeds, or by new payment method when the rider pays it with a newly added payment method.
- The clause *or by refund offset when a refund or fare adjustment is booked against a charge that is still outstanding, in which case the settlement equals the outstanding amount of that charge and the rider's card is not refunded for the part that was never collected* is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis.
- A charge that was collected (one with no payment failure entry booked against it) never gets a settlement entry. Whether a charge has a payment failure entry is read from the system's charge records for that charge.

## Quick reference

| Situation on the charge | Settlement entry possible |
|---|---|
| Collected; no payment failure entry against it | No — never |
| Payment failure entry booked against it; manual retry on the card on file succeeds | Yes — card retry |
| Payment failure entry booked against it; rider pays with a newly added payment method | Yes — new payment method |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A rider has two trips: on the first, a fare of $14.20 failed after the automatic retries and nothing has been settled; on the second, a wait time charge of $1.17 failed and was later settled in full by card retry. The rider's outstanding balance is $14.20: the second trip's failure is matched by its settlement, and the first trip's failure stands.

An outstanding charge is settled in full by one trip_balance_settlement row for that charge

or refund_offset when a refund or fare adjustment is booked against a charge that is still outstanding, in which case the settlement equals the outstanding amount of that charge and the rider's card is not refunded for the part that was never collected
